# The Finding Ledger — lessons with their extensions

<!-- Generated by kstack-init on {{DATE}} for {{PROJECT_NAME}}. This file ships with its
     lesson list EMPTY by design: kstack carries the mechanism; the lessons are minted at
     THIS repo's unit closes, from THIS repo's findings. See kstack's PHILOSOPHY.md ("Why the
     ledger ships empty") for the reasoning. -->

**What this is.** The home of the repo's build lessons, kept in the form Bennett's razor demands
(*"explanations should be no more specific than necessary"* — arXiv:2301.12987): each lesson is
the **weakest statement still sufficient** to correctly decide every finding in its
**extension** (the recorded defects it forbids). AGENTS.md holds the *procedure*; lessons and
their evidence accrete HERE, so the procedure file stays a fixed size.

**How lessons are born.** Only at unit closes (AGENTS.md step 5b), only from local evidence:
when a round's findings are clustered by mechanism, each cluster is looked up here first —

- **Covered but unenforced** — an existing lesson's extension already decides it. The statement
  was right; its MEDIUM failed. Promote the medium (prose → checklist field → lint / Record /
  registry walk / DB trigger). Do not touch the statement.
- **Not covered** — the standing lesson is TOO STRONG. Weaken the statement until the new member
  falls inside, then re-run the sufficiency walk over ALL its members.
- **No lesson claims it** — mint one: the weakest statement sufficient over the cluster AND any
  historical findings it also decides (search the probes — a new lesson usually has older
  members nobody named). Land it in the most quantification-forcing medium that can express it;
  prose-only requires a written reason.

A lesson is never seeded from another repo, this template included: a statement with no local
members has an unrunnable sufficiency walk and undefined regeneration forks — it would be
doctrine wearing no proof, anchored to another codebase's failure distribution.

**The sufficiency walk** keeps this from being taste: for every finding in a claimed extension,
one sentence — "applied at build time, this forbids that defect because …". A member you cannot
write the sentence for is not in the extension.

**The lesson entry form.** Each lesson records: `### Ln — <statement title>`, the statement
itself (one to three sentences, no more specific than necessary), its **Extension** (findings
cited by probe number — plus any positive members: places the lesson is already mechanized and
held), its **Medium**, and its **Status** (stable / promotion queued with a named trigger /
weakened on date, why).

**Media, ranked by quantification force** (why: a Record/walk/trigger can only say "EVERY member
of the family…", which is a weak hypothesis whose extension includes members that do not exist
yet — the reason mechanized lessons hold under attack and prose ones leak):
`DB constraint/trigger` > `registry walk / compile-forced Record` > `lint rule` > `required
design-artifact field` > `gate-rubric line` > `prose (with reason)`.

**The young-ledger bootstrap.** An empty lesson list does not shrink verification to nothing:
until lessons exist, the per-unit sweep (AGENTS.md step 4a) falls back to the generic
falsification classes in `/adversarial-audit`'s seam catalogue as its work breakdown, and the
first closes convert what those rounds actually land into this repo's first lessons. The ledger
then takes over as the sweep's primary breakdown, with the generic catalogue remaining the
completeness floor beneath it.

## Loop health

One row per gated unit, appended by the close-unit step. `novel n/m` = statements minted vs
total findings (the loop's health metric: mostly re-samplings ⇒ the problem is media, not
doctrine). `mode:` = whether the external gate ran FED (ledger in the rubric) or BLIND — the
gate script SELF-SCHEDULES a blind CONTROL round every 4th unit by counting `mode: fed` rows
since the last `mode: blind` row in this table (no human keeps the count; `--with-ledger` /
`--no-ledger` override one run). If blind rounds keep finding what fed rounds stopped finding,
the feed is anchoring (drop the hunt clause, keep the disclosure rule); if both converge on the
same shrinking set, the feed is innocent.

(no rows yet — the first gated unit's close appends the first)

## Ledger discipline

One lesson per statement; extensions cite probes by number; a regenerated finding is FIRST a
diagnosis (which fork above), only then a fix. When a lesson is fully mechanized, its AGENTS.md
prose (if any) is CUT to a one-line pointer — that is the graduation rule that keeps AGENTS.md
from bloating. Unit-close records live in the unit's own probe (§ "Close of unit"); this file
holds only the distilled lessons.
